question: Should OpenClaw add a native ASR/STT backend abstraction now, and should the first slice start with macOS Push-to-Talk while reusing existing Gateway media or Talk provider contracts?
rationale: The missing capability is clear from source, but the safe implementation crosses native app capture, Gateway/provider ownership, SecretRef/auth isolation, private-network policy, fallback UX, and platform scope.

options.title: Design shared seam, start with macOS PTT
options.body: Preserve platform speech by default, use the narrower macOS Push-to-Talk issue as the first implementation slice, and make the provider/security contract reusable for later native surfaces.

options.title: Build broad cross-platform settings
options.body: Add macOS, iOS, Android, and possibly WebChat native ASR settings in one larger project, accepting more design and validation risk up front.

options.title: Defer native ASR core work
options.body: Keep self-hosted STT on existing media, Talk relay, channel, plugin, or sidecar paths until maintainers prioritize a native-app extension point.

recommendation.title: Design shared seam, start with macOS PTT
recommendation.body: Preserve platform speech by default, use the narrower macOS Push-to-Talk issue as the first implementation slice, and make the provider/security contract reusable for later native surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest product-boundary signal for the recommended first slice is the native macOS PTT/Talk and voice overlay/session history.
